0.original: Hythlodaeus is looking you up and down.

25.original: Use the aetheric rope to capture weakened petaloudai.

48.original: In case you didn't know, it's rude to stare. Stop.

49.original: Now then, our friend Hermes. Aside from overseeing the facility, he also conducts his own research.

50.original: Chances are he will be at the main observation hub, so let us seek him out there first.

51.original: Attired as you are, however, you stand out a little too much. Our dear Emet-Selch wishes to keep a low profile for his errand, so...

52.original: Do you know how to make a robe? The basic concept will do.

54.original: No. Your whim, your responsibility. You're getting not another thimble of aether out of me.

55.original: <sigh> The way he scrimps sometimes, you'd think he <hex:021A020203>wasn't<hex:021A020103> a nigh-bottomless font of magic...

56.original: Very well, I shall make the robe, but perhaps you can assist. Come, let us search for the requisite material.

57.original: No means no. Just be grateful I'm even willing to wait.

59.original: An aetheric rope. I want you to use it to capture, shall we say, two petaloudai.

60.original: There are three species here, I believe. Any two different kinds should serve.

61.original: Now, I should mention that the strength of the rope is tied─no pun intended─to the strength of its user.

62.original: As your aether is still thin compared to ours, you'll need to weaken the petaloudai first. Good luck!

63.original: Remember, it's a pair of petaloudai we require. Any two different kinds should serve.

64.original: You've caught the petaloudai? Come, come, let us see.

65.original: Yes, these fine fellows will do nicely. And now for a spot of reversion...

67.original: It's nothing fancy, but then we're trying <hex:021A020203>not<hex:021A020103> to stand out. Try it on for size.

69.original: You turn living beings into clothing? Just like that?

70.original: Won't someone be angry with us for using those creatures?

71.original: Well, not <hex:021A020203>just<hex:021A020103> like that. You need to revert them to their constituent aether first.

72.original: Lest you wonder why I asked for two species, it is due to the difference in their aetheric balance. Blending them allows us to produce garb with superior aetheric stability.

73.original: Oh, it's fine, there's no one around to tell us off. And besides, we can always make more petaloudai. They need only a tiny amount of aether.

74.original: It may take some effort to get the form and composition right, but anyone familiar with the concept should be able to manage.

75.original: Well and good to disguise <hex:021A020203>and<hex:021A020103> educate it, but it won't fool anyone who can see worth a damn.

76.original: Fair point, but at the very least it should spare you unwanted attention from casual observers.

77.original: Emet-Selch speaks true. Even dressed like us, your unusual nature will be plain to those who think to look.

78.original: Should someone question your presence, don't make up excuses, much less try to explain what you actually are. No, best to simply say that you're a familiar.

80.original: Ah, of course─Azem's. If you say you belong to <hex:02080DE905FF04686572FF0468696D03>, people will give you the benefit of the doubt for any and all outlandish behavior.

82.original: For lack of <hex:02080DE905FF04686572FF0468697303> presence, absolutely. Were <hex:02080CE905FF04736865FF03686503> here, <hex:02080CE905FF04736865FF03686503>'d have been the first to propose the idea─and you know it.

83.original: With that, your story is settled. Let us continue with our errand!
